name: application-stepper-wizard
title: Stepper Wizard
description: Multi-step form flow with a progress header, back/next controls, and a per-step content slot, driven by a typed steps prop contract.
useWhen: A form is long enough to benefit from being broken into focused, sequential steps.
Users need to see overall progress (completed, current, upcoming) across an onboarding or checkout flow.
Each step has distinct fields or validation and should not overwhelm the user in a single view.
avoidWhen: The form is short enough to complete in one screen — a single form is faster than paging through steps.
Steps must be completed out of order — this pattern assumes a linear progression.
You only need a static progress indicator with no interactive back/next flow — use the simpler `steps` component.
responsiveBehavior: The step header wraps to smaller connector widths on narrow viewports; the body content and footer actions stay full-width within the card.
accessibility: The current step's indicator carries aria-current='step' so assistive tech announces progress accurately.
Completed steps use a checkmark icon plus a filled background, not color alone, to signal completion.
The Back button exposes a disabled state on the first step rather than being hidden, keeping focus order stable.

variants.title: Stepper Wizard
variants.description: Three-step billing wizard with a progress header (complete/current/upcoming), a form body slot, and back/continue actions.
accessibility: Each step label stays visible alongside its indicator so the flow doesn't rely on numbers or color alone.

variants.title: Stepper Wizard (Dark)
variants.description: Multi-step wizard adapted for dark surfaces with the same progress header, body slot, and action structure.
accessibility: Step connector lines and label text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
